description: A feature flag returning an integer `N>0` made the checkout service's `sendToKafka` fan every `OrderResult` out into `1 + N` identical copies on the `orders` Kafka topic (all sharing the same `order_id`); the accounting service's `Consumer.cs` inserted each copy into `accounting.order` whose primary key is `order_id`, so every duplicate beyond the first raised Postgres SQLSTATE `23505` `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "order_pkey"` (logged as EF Core errors in the accounting service), and the fraud-detection consumer slept an additional 1 second per message.
mechanism:
The `kafkaQueueProblems` feature flag is read by the **checkout** service inside `sendToKafka` ([`src/checkout/main.go:683-693`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/checkout/main.go#L683-L693)). When `getIntFeatureFlag(ctx, "kafkaQueueProblems")` returns an integer `N > 0`, checkout logs `"FeatureFlag 'kafkaQueueProblems' is activated, overloading queue now."` and then spawns `N` goroutines that each re-publish the same `OrderResult` to the `orders` Kafka topic, producing `1 + N` copies of every placed order with the same `order_id`. In parallel, the **fraud-detection** consumer reads the same flag inside its poll loop ([`fraud-detection/src/main/kotlin/frauddetection/main.kt:60-62`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/fraud-detection/src/main/kotlin/frauddetection/main.kt#L60-L62)) and calls `Thread.sleep(1000)` for every record it polls, capping its consumer throughput at ~1 record/s and amplifying lag on the `orders` topic.

The downstream consumer of interest is the **accounting** service ([`src/accounting/Consumer.cs`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/accounting/Consumer.cs)). `StartListening` ([`Consumer.cs:55-83`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/accounting/Consumer.cs#L55-L83)) runs a synchronous loop that, for each Kafka record, opens an `order-consumed` activity (line 65) and calls `ProcessMessage` ([`Consumer.cs:86-138`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/accounting/Consumer.cs#L86-L138)). `ProcessMessage` constructs an `OrderEntity` with `Id = order.OrderId` (lines 99-102) and calls `dbContext.Add(orderEntity)` (line 103). Because `OrderEntity` declares `[PrimaryKey(nameof(Id))]` with `[Column("order_id")]` ([`Entities.cs:52-58`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/accounting/Entities.cs#L52-L58)), EF Core's in-memory change tracker maintains a per-`DBContext` identity map keyed by `Id`. The first copy of any duplicated order succeeds; every subsequent copy hits `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.ChangeTracking.Internal.IdentityMap<TKey>.ThrowIdentityConflict` and raises `System.InvalidOperationException: The instance of entity type 'OrderEntity' cannot be tracked because another instance with the same key value for {'Id'} is already being tracked.`. The exception is caught by `ProcessMessage`'s try/catch ([`Consumer.cs:135-138`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/accounting/Consumer.cs#L135-L138)) and logged as the Error-severity record `"Order parsing failed:"`. Because the conflict is detected at EF Core's change-tracking layer before the batched INSERT is built, no SQL ever reaches Postgres — so no SQLSTATE `23505` `order_pkey` violation, no `accounting:otel` DB span ERROR, and no row insert succeeds for the duplicated `order_id`.

variants.description: Fraud-detection container network receive rate spiked in bursts (from ~400 to peaks of ~4000 bytes/s) as it consumed duplicate order messages from the Kafka orders topic in irregular bursts due to the 1-second sleep per record.
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident baseline is approximately 397-415 bytes/sec. At 15:22 UTC (first reading after incident time 15:21:17), the value jumps to 494.862, roughly 80+ above the baseline ceiling, marking the clear start of the spike that continues escalating to 1600+.

variants.description: Fraud-detection container network transmit rate tripled (from ~1000 to ~3000 bytes/s) because the fraud-detection consumer's Thread.sleep(1000) per record slowed consumption, causing accumulated telemetry to be sent in larger batches.
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident baseline hovers around 960-1050 bytes/s. At 15:22, the value jumps to ~1149, clearly breaking above the baseline range, and then rapidly climbs to ~3000 over the next several minutes. This is the first timestamp after the incident where the spike begins.

variants.description: Accounting container network receive rate doubled (from ~480 to ~1100+ bytes/s) because the accounting consumer received duplicate order messages on the Kafka orders topic, produced by checkout's overload goroutines.
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident baseline is roughly 475-498. At 15:22, one minute after the incident marker, the value jumps to ~583, a clear departure (~19% above the highest baseline value). It continues rising sharply to ~800+ and then ~1200+ in subsequent minutes, confirming the spike onset at 15:22.

variants.description: OpenSearch container network receive rate doubled (from ~10K to ~22K bytes/s) because it ingested the surge of error logs from accounting (InvalidOperationException) and info logs from fraud-detection (sleep messages) forwarded by the OTel collector.
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident baseline fluctuates around 9,500–10,500. At 15:22, the value jumps to 12,149.8, clearly breaking above the baseline range, and continues climbing rapidly to ~25,000+ in subsequent minutes. This is the first post-incident timestamp with a significant departure from baseline.

variants.description: Offset commit rate for fraud-detection consumer. Collapsed from ~0.21 commits/s to near 0 because the consumer rarely completes a poll cycle (blocked by per-record sleeps), so it almost never commits offsets.
variants.onset_reasoning: The metric holds steady around 0.2088-0.2089 through 15:22. At 15:23 it drops sharply to 0.0696, then to 0.0315 at 15:24, and reaches zero at 15:25 where it remains. The last timestamp showing the pre-incident active level is 15:22, making it the onset of the collapse.

This is direct textual confirmation that the kafkaQueueProblems flag is on and is the primary driver of fraud-detection consumer lag.
logs.cause: Direct effect of kafkaQueueProblems. When `getFeatureFlagValue("kafkaQueueProblems") > 0`, the fraud-detection consumer loop at `fraud-detection/src/main/kotlin/frauddetection/main.kt:60-62` logs this line and calls `Thread.sleep(1000)` for every polled record, capping consumer throughput at ~1 record/s regardless of producer volume.

logs.name: accounting — "Order parsing failed:" InvalidOperationException EF Core duplicate-Id (ERROR)
logs.description: Between 15:21:30.881 and 15:30:56.168 UTC, the accounting service logged 1200 Error-severity `Order parsing failed:` entries. Each entry carries `exception.type=InvalidOperationException` whose message is `The instance of entity type 'OrderEntity' cannot be tracked because another instance with the same key value for {'Id'} is already being tracked.` and whose stacktrace ends at `Accounting.Consumer.ProcessMessage(...) in /src/Accounting/Consumer.cs:line 102` (the `dbContext.Add(orderEntity)` call). This is the dominant application-level Error-severity signal in the capture.
logs.cause: Cascading effect of kafkaQueueProblems via checkout. Checkout's overload loop (`checkout/main.go:683-693`) re-publishes the same `OrderResult` message to the `orders` topic ffValue extra times, producing duplicate copies with the same `order_id`. The accounting consumer (`Accounting.Consumer.ProcessMessage` at `accounting/Consumer.cs:103`) calls `dbContext.Add(orderEntity)` for each copy with `Id = order.OrderId`. EF Core's in-memory change tracker (`IdentityMap.ThrowIdentityConflict`) detects the duplicate primary key and throws `InvalidOperationException` before any SQL ever reaches Postgres — so no Postgres `23505` / `order_pkey` violation is observable in this capture.

logs.name: kafka broker — GroupCoordinator consumer-group rebalance for `accounting` (INFO)
logs.description: Between 15:23:27.687 and 15:24:07.949 UTC, the Kafka broker's GroupCoordinator logged 5 rebalance-related INFO events for the `accounting` consumer group: a new dynamic member joining, the group entering PreparingRebalance, the previous member being removed after failing its session heartbeat, the group stabilizing on a new generation, and the assignment being received from the new leader. These events occur a few minutes after the flag was toggled on, once the accounting consumer's exception-storm loop has stalled long enough to miss heartbeats.
logs.cause: Downstream effect of kafkaQueueProblems. The accounting consumer's `ProcessMessage` (`accounting/Consumer.cs:86-138`) runs synchronously inside the consume loop and throws an EF Core `InvalidOperationException` on every duplicate order message produced by checkout's overload loop. The cumulative slowdown — combined with fraud-detection's 1-second-per-record sleep on the same `orders` topic — causes accounting's librdkafka client to miss session heartbeats, so the broker removes the member and triggers a rebalance of `group accounting` (group id set on `accounting/Consumer.cs:145`).
